tldr: DeepSeek's retrained V4-Flash beat flagship V4 Pro on nine agent benchmarks in late July, released amid an intensifying China AI price war, before going fully open-source. A week of price-hike warnings led into V4 Pro's confirmed Aug 13 launch at sharply higher prices alongside Harness, DeepSeek's open-source Claude Code rival, now at v0.1 under an MIT license and wrapping Claude Code and Codex as its own sub-agents.
whats_new: A Chinese security firm disclosed a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Harness on Aug 25 — DeepSeek's open-source coding-agent tool's first disclosed security failure, with patch status not yet reported.
why_it_matters: Harness now calls Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents, so evaluate it as a scheduling layer, not just a rival, before standardizing on it. The Aug 25 RCE disclosure is Harness's first hard security signal — don't run its plugin ecosystem against production credentials until a fix is confirmed. The underlying V4 Pro price hike still stands despite the weekend-surcharge rollback.

status.state: Harness's first security flaw disclosed Aug 25; V4 Pro price hike still stands post-rollback
status.detail: Harness open-sourced alongside V4 Pro's Aug 13 launch, reached China's supercomputing network Aug 15, hit v0.1 under an MIT license Aug 17, and began wrapping Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents Aug 20-21. QiAnXin disclosed a critical RCE flaw in it Aug 25, with no confirmed fix yet. DeepSeek ended the weekend price surcharge Aug 23, even as cumulative prices remain up 355%.

beats.headline: Price-hike reports build for over a week, alongside the earliest coding-tool rumors, and a hands-on already finds cracks in the "cheaper" pitch
beats.summary: Memeburn previews "DeepSeek Code" a week before any official word. Bloomberg, Investing.com, TechNode, and regional coverage flag a coming price increase for over a week before V4 Pro's launch makes it real. The-decoder.com's Aug 12 check still finds DeepSeek beating MAI Code on price; The New Stack's Aug 10 hands-on finds the "better and cheaper" promise holds only partly.

beats.headline: DeepSeek publicizes a dedicated team building agent tools to rival Claude Code
beats.summary: A Pi-founder claim that DeepSeek plus Pi already beats Claude Code opens the day; hours later Bloomberg is first to report DeepSeek forming a team aimed squarely at Anthropic's Claude Code, corroborated same-day by PYMNTS' "new team" framing and repeated by briefs.co and TradingView into Aug 13 — hours before that team's tool ships.

beats.headline: A wave of Qwen 3.8 coverage and same-keyword noise rides the shared search cluster
beats.summary: Not part of the DeepSeek story: ten Qwen 3.8 pieces (release, hardware runs, comparisons vs. Kimi K3/GPT-5.6/Claude Opus), two Anthropic blog posts about Claude Cowork, and an unrelated open-source project also calling itself an agent "harness" all get swept in by the shared "open weight"/"Claude Code"/"harness" search cluster. Flagged for transparency, not narrative continuity.

beats.headline: A quiet OpenRouter build becomes DeepSeek's officially confirmed V4 Pro release, at sharply higher prices
beats.summary: Simon Willison spots the refreshed Pro model listed API-only with no announcement page; a day later, Lufkin Daily News, Reuters, The Information, and Global Times confirm it as a deliberate release at sharply higher user prices, with The Information framing it as a direct challenge to Kimi K3.

beats.headline: DeepSeek open-sources Harness, and coverage explodes across a dozen outlets before it reaches v0.1 under an MIT license
beats.summary: VentureBeat first reports the free Harness tool shipping alongside pricier V4-Pro; CGTN and Global Times repeat the framing, with Global Times noting both went live on China's state supercomputing network. The New Stack, 36Kr, TechNode, SCMP, HPCwire, and The Register pile on over the same week. By Aug 17, GuruFocus and MarkTechPost confirm Harness hit v0.1 under an MIT license.

beats.headline: Recap widens to a US-China AI-race frame, quantifies the hike, then pits V4 Pro's price and capability against Qwen 3.8 Max
beats.summary: Coverage widens: benchmark gains cited, the hike framed as a strategy shift and a US-China race, Forbes quantifies it at 14x the cheapest model, and TheSequence reviews it alongside GLM-5.3 and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Willison's Artificial Analysis check puts Qwen 3.8 27B one point behind V4 Pro — DeepSeek's open-weight edge is thin. Memeburn reframes the hike against Qwen 3.8 Max.

beats.headline: Harness adds Claude Code and Codex as pluggable sub-agents, repositioning itself as a scheduling layer rather than a straight rival
beats.summary: A major post-beta update ships 14 changes adding multimodal and subagent support; days later 36Kr reports Harness integrating Claude Code and Codex themselves as callable sub-agents, aiming to become the core scheduling layer above rival tools rather than just a replacement for them.

beats.headline: DeepSeek ships V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, its first multimodal model pitched against Opus 4.8
beats.summary: Eight outlets corroborate the vision-capable model over two days — Seeking Alpha and Investing.com first, then Cryptonews ties it to reported IPO speculation, oodaloop and the-decoder frame it against Opus 4.8's agent-benchmark performance, and Tech in Asia confirms the vision-capable test build a day later with no new capability claims.

beats.headline: DeepSeek drops its weekend peak-pricing surcharge, even as cumulative peak prices remain up sharply
beats.summary: Bloomberg and a second outlet report DeepSeek ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge for API users the same day a comparison piece puts cumulative peak-price increases at 355% since the original hike — an incremental de-escalation, not a reversal of the underlying V4 Pro price increase.

beats.headline: A Chinese security firm discloses a critical RCE flaw in Harness, days after a still-unconfirmed second multimodal model
beats.summary: TahawulTech.com alone reports a second multimodal model Aug 24, still unnamed a day later. A plugin-architecture deep dive on Harness runs the same day; the next day QiAnXin discloses a critical remote-code-execution vulnerability in Harness itself, and a same-day retrospective revisits open source's early pioneers — the first hard failure evidence in Harness's three-week rollout.

open_questions: Is the Aug 24 "new multimodal model" a distinct release from V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, or delayed/duplicate coverage of the same Aug 21 launch — what's the model's actual name and spec?
Has QiAnXin's disclosed RCE flaw in Harness been assigned a CVE or fixed in a specific version, and has DeepSeek published a security advisory?

Now that Harness can invoke Claude Code and Codex as sub-agents, does that require users to supply their own Anthropic/OpenAI credentials, and what does that mean for the "free Claude Code rival" framing?
Does V4 Pro's claimed "agent gains" reclaim the benchmark lead V4-Flash took in July, or does Flash remain the stronger agent option?
Forbes prices V4 Pro at 14x DeepSeek's cheapest model — is that still cheaper than Qwen 3.8 Max per token, or has DeepSeek lost its price edge to Alibaba?
Does ending the weekend peak-pricing surcharge signal a broader course-correction on pricing, or is it a narrow carve-out that leaves the underlying V4 Pro hike intact?
take_for_builders: Treat Harness as unpatched until DeepSeek or QiAnXin confirms a fix for the disclosed RCE flaw — don't run it against production credentials or untrusted plugins yet. Hold off on any DeepSeek multimodal comparison until a second outlet names the Aug 24 model. Re-check weekend/off-peak API rates before locking a cost model.
